interactions.summary: Jiang says the shadow excites Dante because it means fans will swarm him again, compares that addiction to celebrity and social-media metrics, a student says public attention consumes people until they destroy themselves, and Jiang agrees that fame makes the life empty and narcissistic.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang monologue with student extension and Jiang confirmation

interactions.summary: A student reads the next passage in which Virgil and Dante meet the solitary Lombard soul Sordello, who responds warmly once he learns Virgil is from Mantua too.
Jiang identifies Sordello as a major troubadour poet from Virgil's region, notes Virgil's enthusiasm at meeting a compatriot, and has the class continue into Dante's political lament over Italy.

claims.claim: Jiang's reading is that Dante cares about the shadow because it guarantees more admirers, autographs, and fame rather than progress toward Beatrice, God, or heaven.
Jiang generalizes Dante's condition into a modern celebrity model: influencers become trapped by metrics, subscriptions, and ratings, forever chasing more attention.
Jiang concludes that fame makes a person egotistical and narcissistic because the prized shadow is only an illusion, so a life centered on it is empty.
The next read-aloud introduces Sordello as a fellow Mantuan whose shared homeland is enough to produce an immediate embrace with Virgil.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted text and lecture explanation given on 2026-06-25.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang makes Dante's desire brutally simple: forget Beatrice and heaven, he wants his shadow because it brings his fans back.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the lecture's most vivid condensation of Dante's fame addiction.

signature_moments.moment: The influencer analogy translates Dante's spiritual vanity into a modern economy of subscriptions, views, and endless metric hunger.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the metrics, the number of subscriptions you have
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It links medieval fame addiction to a familiar contemporary pathology.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang says the thing Dante lives for is literally a shadow, which exposes the emptiness of the fame itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: all he cares about now is his shadow
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The image preserves the moral force of the scene without abstraction.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's reading of Dante as someone hooked on the public attention that follows his visible sign, even though that sign is only a shadow.
Jiang's classification of Sordello as a major love poet in the courtly-love tradition.

chronology_notes.note: The packet completes Jiang's attack on Dante's fame hunger and then pivots into the Sordello encounter that opens the canto's larger political meditation on Italy.
